hook.text: 'The White House announced today...' A building can't talk—but you know exactly what it means.

buildup.text: Metonymy uses one entity to stand for a related one: container for contents, place for institution.

discovery.text: 'Lend me a hand' (hand for help), 'new blood' (blood for people)—metonymy is everywhere.

twist.text: Metonymy is not metaphor: metaphor maps across domains; metonymy stays within one domain.

climax.text: Both are cognitive shortcuts that compress complex ideas into compact expressions.

punchline.text: Name one thing and let it stand for another.

quiz.question: How does metonymy differ from metaphor?
options: Metonymy links related things in one domain
